tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. - `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

"""Checkpoints and the raw evidence space (D-041).

GET /api/checkpoints            the two checkpoints, what each makes visible, and the acquire run lineage
GET /api/scan/points            every customer comment as a point (fixed 3D layout) with its first checkpoint
GET /api/scan/comment/{id}      one comment, verbatim, with its provenance
GET /api/scan/sources?cp=       the other raw sources visible at a checkpoint (study, sales, options, research, web)
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re

from fastapi import APIRouter, Query

from api.deps import db, not_found
from bmw_req.checkpoints import BY_ID, CHECKPOINTS, latest_run, visible_ids

router = APIRouter(prefix="/api", tags=["scan"])

CARS = ["F70", "G60", "G68", "G70"]
MARKETS = ["EU", "US", "CN", "RoW"]
CHANNELS = ["Source A", "Source B", "Source C", "Source D"]
ENGINES = ["ICE", "PHEV", "BEV"]
TYPES = ["Likes", "Wants", "Difficult to Use", "Defect", None]   # BMW's own label (first one), None = unlabelled
KINDS = ["feedback", "study", "sales", "option_list", "research", "web", "reference"]


# Research that is about one of our car lines moves from the date ring onto that car's rings (D-042):
# public sales figures → sales ring, ratings/reviews/studies → study ring, product news → options ring.
CAR_PATTERNS = {"G70": r"7 Series|\bi7\b|\bG70\b|\bG11\b|\bG12\b", "G60": r"5 Series|\bi5\b|\bG60\b|\bG68\b|\bG30\b",
                "F70": r"1 Series|\bF70\b|\bF40\b"}
SALES_METRICS = {"deliveries", "registrations", "retail_sales", "market_share"}


def research_cars(entity: str | None, headline: str) -> list[str]:
    """Car lines an item is about: by its entity, or by its headline when the entity is BMW as a whole."""
    ent = entity or ""
    hit = [c for c, p in CAR_PATTERNS.items() if re.search(p, ent)]
    if not hit and ent.strip() in ("BMW", "BMW AG", "BMW Group"):
        hit = [c for c, p in CAR_PATTERNS.items() if re.search(p, headline)]
    return hit


def research_ring(meta: dict) -> str:
    if meta.get("metric") in SALES_METRICS:
        return "sales"
    if meta.get("topic") == "consumer_studies" or meta.get("kind") == "study":
        return "study"
    return "options"


def _cp(cp: str) -> str:
    if cp not in BY_ID:
        raise not_found(f"No checkpoint {cp!r}; use one of {', '.join(BY_ID)}")
    return cp


@router.get("/checkpoints")
def checkpoints() -> list[dict]:
@router.get("/scan/sources")
def sources(cp: str = Query("cp2")) -> dict:
    """Everything that is not a comment, visible at `cp`; `new` marks what this checkpoint added over its parent."""
    cp = _cp(cp)
    vis = visible_ids(cp)
    q = ",".join("?" * len(vis))
    with db() as conn:
        sales = [dict(r) for r in conn.execute(
            f"""SELECT sa.vehicle_model_id car, sa.market_code market, sa.year, sa.units, sa.is_forecast
                FROM sales sa JOIN source_item s ON s.id = sa.source_item_id WHERE s.checkpoint IN ({q})
                ORDER BY 1, 2, 3""", vis)]
        study = [dict(r) for r in conn.execute(
            f"""SELECT m.id, m.vehicle_model_id car, m.market_code market, m.scale, m.item,
                       ROUND(m.z_within_column, 3) z, ROUND(COALESCE(m.mean, m.top2), 3) value
                FROM study_metric m JOIN source_item s ON s.id = m.source_item_id WHERE s.checkpoint IN ({q})
                ORDER BY m.vehicle_model_id, m.market_code, m.z_within_column DESC""", vis)]
        options = []
        for r in conn.execute(f"""SELECT id, vehicle_model_id car, external_id code, meta_json FROM source_item
                                  WHERE kind = 'option_list' AND checkpoint IN ({q}) ORDER BY vehicle_model_id, id""", vis):
            m = json.loads(r["meta_json"] or "{}")
            options.append({"id": r["id"], "car": r["car"], "code": r["code"], "name": m.get("name_en"),
                            "category": m.get("category"), "availability": m.get("availability"),
                            "package": m.get("package_name")})
        research = []
        for r in conn.execute(
                f"""SELECT id, market_code market, trust_tier tier, published_at, text, url, meta_json,
                           checkpoint = ? AS is_new
                    FROM source_item WHERE kind = 'research' AND checkpoint IN ({q}) ORDER BY published_at""",
                (cp, *vis)):
            m = json.loads(r["meta_json"] or "{}")
            headline = r["text"].split(" — ")[0]
            cars = research_cars(m.get("entity"), headline)
            research.append({"id": r["id"], "cars": cars, "ring": research_ring(m) if cars else None,
                             "market": r["market"], "region": m.get("region"), "tier": r["tier"],
                             "topic": m.get("topic"), "kind": m.get("kind"), "entity": m.get("entity"),
                             "published_at": r["published_at"], "headline": headline,
                             "yoy": m.get("yoy_pct"), "value": m.get("value"), "unit": m.get("unit"),
                             "pair_key": m.get("pair_key"), "url": r["url"], "new": bool(r["is_new"])})
        web = conn.execute(f"SELECT COUNT(*) n, SUM(checkpoint = ?) new FROM source_item WHERE kind = 'web' "
                           f"AND checkpoint IN ({q})", (cp, *vis)).fetchone()
    return {"checkpoint": cp, "sales": sales, "study": study, "options": options, "research": research,
            "web": {"n": web["n"] or 0, "new": web["new"] or 0}}

132:The whole interface is a scan volume. A true-black field holds every piece of raw evidence as a contact in one fixed 3D space; each checkpoint is a sweep that passes through that space, and the screen shows what the sweep acquired and how existing tracks changed. The 3D canvas is the page. Everything else sits at the edges of the volume: the readout, the filter chips and the checkpoint timeline as frameless text and marks straight on the black, the inspector and the hover card as small sheets of tinted glass, so the evidence is never boxed into cards or framed by chrome.
133-
134-Density sits in the contacts, not in the text. Numerals carry the information, set wide, light and tabular like instrument readouts; words are short labels. The only running text is the customer's own words, shown in the inspector at reading size. Colour is categorical and earned: each raw data type has its own hue, one blue belongs to the sweep and the PM's current position, and amber is held back for loss. State is carried by mark shape, never by hue alone.
135-
136-Motion is a single event, not ambience. The volume never turns by itself; it moves only when the PM drags it. The sweep plays once on arrival and once on each checkpoint change, and contacts it passes flare white as they are acquired.

138-**Key Characteristics:**
139-- True black ground (#000) with the live 3D canvas full-bleed behind every overlay.
140:- Overlays pinned to the 24px edge: readout with the filter chips under it top-left, checkpoint timeline bottom-right (both frameless), inspector top-right (glass).
141-- Wide, light, tabular numerals as the primary text.
142-- Five categorical data-type hues, one sweep blue, amber reserved for loss.
143-- Mark shape encodes track state: dot = held, ring = acquired by this sweep.
144-- One sweep per checkpoint change; no idle motion of the volume.
145-
146-## Colors
147-
148-A black instrument field with white ink, five categorical data hues validated on black, and two reserved signals: sweep blue and loss amber.
149-
150-### Primary
151:- **Sweep Blue** (sweep, sweep-hi, sweep-wash): the sweep and the PM's position. The deep step colours the sweep blade's additive wash; the bright step draws the blade's leading edge, the active checkpoint node (with a 4px sweep-wash halo), the border of a filter chip in use, a chosen filter value's bar, the focus ring, links and text selection.
152-
153-### Secondary
154-- **Loss Amber** (lost-amber): reserved for weakened and lost tracks, which appear from the clustering stage on. Raw sources are only ever acquired, so the scan surface uses amber only for the failed-scan message (a lost signal).
155-
156-### Tertiary (categorical, one hue per raw data type)
157-- **Comment Blue** (type-comment): customer verbatims, the galaxy at the centre of the volume.
158-- **Research Vermilion** (type-research): cited web research on the dated outer ring.
159-- **Study Aqua** (type-study): customer-study ticks on the innermost range ring.
160-- **Option Ochre** (type-option): price-list equipment on the options ring.
161-- **Sales Magenta** (type-sales): BMW sales volumes on the sales ring; forecasts render as wireframe outlines in the same hue.
162-
163-The same hue colours the data type's inline legend glyph wherever the type is named (readout, ring name tags, inspector header).
164-
165-### Neutral
166-- **Void** (void): the page and the WebGL clear colour. Never a near-black; pure black is what makes the contacts read as emitters.
167-- **Smoked Glass** (glass): every floating panel, always with a backdrop blur over the canvas.
168-- **Hairline** (hair) and **Strong Hairline** (hair-strong): panel borders, chip outlines, filter bar tracks, the checkpoint rail, the z-bar midline, scrollbars, mobile pill outlines.
169-- **Ink** (ink): numerals, titles, the customer quote, active labels, the held mark.
170-- **Ink 2** (ink-2): secondary values, filter names and counts, ring labels, the checkpoint fill.
171-- **Ink 3** (ink-3): micro labels, inactive tabs and nodes, meta lines. Holds at least 4.5:1 on black; it is the floor for any text.
172-
173-In 3D, range rings are white at 10% opacity and the time ring is a white dashed line at 22%.
174-
175-### Named Rules
176-**The One Blue Rule.** Sweep blue means "the sweep, or where the PM is right now". It never fills a data series and never decorates.

196-- **Micro** (400, 11px, 0.02em, ink-3): field and readout labels, legend names, ring sublabels; at 600 with 0.1em tracking it labels the time ring.

content.content:
238:### Filter Chips
239-A row of chips directly under the readout, one per dimension, any number active at once (values within a dimension are alternatives, dimensions combine).
240-- **At rest:** only the chips in use, each showing its dimension in ink-3, the chosen value in ink (first value, "+n" for more) and an ×; a sweep-hi hairline border marks them as set. After them a quiet "Filter" hint (sliders icon, ink-3). Nothing else is drawn, so the readout stays the focus.
241-- **Hover:** hovering the row reveals the unused chips after the ones in use (never before them, so chips in use don't move) and a "Clear all · Esc" text button. Hovering a chip opens its values in a glass list hanging under it: a micro scope line (what this dimension filters), then rows of name, a 2px bar and a tabular count; chosen rows in ink with a sweep-hi bar. Choosing a value closes the list again, so only the choice stays on the chip. Counts already apply the other active filters.
242-- **Chips:** 28px pills, hairline border on a 60% black fill, 12px ink-2 text. Car and Market filter every data type. The others belong to one type and carry its glyph: Channel, Label and Engine (comments), Trust (web research), Study result (above / around / below the car × market's average by half a standard deviation), Category (equipment options), Sales year (2024, 2025, 2030 forecast). entries.description:
Use a mouse and keyboard to interact with a web browser, and take screenshots. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.
* Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element before moving the cursor.
* If you tried clicking on a program or link but it failed to load, even after waiting, try adjusting your click location so that the tip of the cursor visually falls on the element that you want to click.
* Make sure to click any buttons, links, icons, etc with the cursor tip in the center of the element. Don't click boxes on their edges unless asked.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported and will return an error - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels. content.text:
The filter row on the Evidence (Scan) page is now always visible. A collapse button at the start of the row hides the unused filters, and the same button brings them back to the right. I checked it in the running app: it collapses and expands, and picking Topic → "China · market" brought web research down from 935 to 77. The type-check passes.

**How it behaves**
- Every filter chip is always shown. Filters you've set stay first, so they never jump around.
- Collapsing hides only the filters you haven't set. Set filters stay visible so nothing is filtered without you seeing it. The collapsed button reads "Filter · 13" (the number of hidden filters).
- The browser remembers whether you left the row collapsed or expanded.
- "Clear all · Esc" appears whenever any filter is set.

**New filters** (all from data the page already loads, so no backend change):

| Filter | Applies to | Values |
|---|---|---|
| Length | Customer comments | Short (under 80 characters, ~2.3k), medium (80–250, ~5.1k), long (250+, ~2.7k). "Long" is a quick way to find detailed comments. |
| Topic | Web research | 11 topics, e.g. BMW, EV challengers, premium competitors, China · market |
| Fact type | Web research | Figure, event, study or rating, policy, trend |
| Availability | Equipment options | Standard, optional, in a package |

I left out a study "scale" filter because the scale just follows the market, so it would repeat the Market filter.

**Working with the other two sessions:** Before starting, I checked with both. One owns page 2 and the 3D scene code. The other built the original filter bar and asked me to keep the "no jumping" chip order, which I did. I didn't touch any of their files. Both have been told what changed.

content.text:
Only partly. The Structure page's audit trail is separated by checkpoint; the Evidence trail and the "Everything" tab are not. I checked the live feed (`api/routers/audit_feed.py`) for both checkpoints:

| Audit view | JAN 26 selected | JUL 26 selected | Separated? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Structure** | 369 JAN rows + 40 untagged | 246 JUL rows + the same 40 untagged | Yes, mostly |
| **Evidence** | 6 JAN + 6 JUL + 106 untagged | the same list | No, the checkpoint is ignored |
| **Everything** | both checkpoints | both checkpoints | No, but each row shows a JAN 26 / JUL 26 tag |

What's behind the gaps:

- **The 40 untagged Structure rows** are the A/B test of the classifier, run before the real classification of either checkpoint. They belong to neither checkpoint, so they appear under both with no label. They should either be labelled "A/B test" or hidden.
- **The Evidence view** only filters by checkpoint on the Structure page. So both checkpoints' data-capture rows show regardless of which checkpoint is selected. Most of the other 106 rows (data loads and research agents) were recorded before checkpoints existed, so they have no checkpoint to filter by. Showing them under both is arguably right, but they could be grouped as "before checkpoints".
- Everything else is tagged correctly: classify, cluster and requirement-area rows carry their checkpoint. One thing to know: the JAN 26 "contextualize" run (run 12) is still marked as running.

The fix would be small. On Evidence, show only the selected checkpoint's capture rows plus the untagged loads, and mark the A/B rows so they stop showing up under both checkpoints. lines: ### Audit Trail
- **Button:** top-right at the edge, a 28px pill like the filter chips (history icon + "Audit", 12px ink-2 on 60% black with a hairline border; ink with a stronger hairline while open).

- **Field:** no card. The trail sits on a frameless black field (86% with a 10px blur) that feathers out at all four edges through a mask, 440px wide, 46px below the edge like the inspector, so it reads as part of the black rather than a box on top of it.

-- **Head:** "Audit trail" (12px/600) and one ink-3 line saying what the view holds; scope tabs in the filter-tab style (the current page, or Everything); then "who acted" chips (24px pills with the actor's mark and a count) that show or hide AI, System and PM rows.

+- **Head:** "Audit trail" (12px/600) and one ink-3 line saying what the view holds; scope tabs in the filter-tab style (the current page, or Everything); then "who acted" chips (24px pills with the actor's mark and a count) that show or hide AI, System and PM rows. The page scope holds only the selected checkpoint ("Evidence · JAN 26"); Everything holds both, each row tagged JAN 26 / JUL 26 (or A/B TEST), and ends with a "Show history before the checkpoint rebuild" text button.

- **Trail:** one hairline rail down the left, day lines pinned at the top while scrolling. Marks on the rail say who acted: AI a hollow ring, System a small ink-3 dot, PM a filled ink dot (the only filled one, because the human decides); a stage starting or finishing is a larger ink ring and its line is set in ink as a milestone. Each row: the line in 12px ink-2, a micro meta line beneath (who · model · steps · time or time range), the checkpoint in micro caps at the right.

- **Folding:** identical steps of one stream (same action, stage and checkpoint, no gap over 10 minutes) fold into one row with their totals ("Classified 2,800 comments → 4,597 signals · 140 steps · 05:31–05:49"), even while another run's steps interleave; a stage milestone closes its streams. A chevron opens the fold into its single steps on a nested hairline. A fold that runs on into rows not loaded yet says "Latest:" and "140+ steps" rather than passing a partial total off as the total.
- **Never blue:** who acted is never coloured; blue is the sweep and the PM's position.

.hovercard-meta { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; font-size: var(--t-micro); color: var(--ink-3); }

-.sheet { position: fixed; top: calc(var(--edge) + 46px); right: var(--edge); z-index: 25; width: min(400px, calc(100vw - 32px)); max-height: calc(100vh - 2 * var(--edge) - 196px); overflow: auto; padding: 28px 26px 24px; border-radius: var(--r); background: var(--glass); border: 1px solid var(--hair); backdrop-filter: blur(16px); -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(16px); box-shadow: 0 2px 6px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5), 0 24px 60px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.6); display: grid; gap: 22px; animation: sheet-in var(--med) var(--ease); }
+/* the inspector: same frameless dark field as the audit trail and the dock (no box, border or shadow); it feathers out
+   at its edges, so content scrolling past the top or bottom fades into the volume instead of being cut */
+.sheet {
+  position: fixed; top: calc(var(--edge) + 46px); right: var(--edge); z-index: 25; width: min(440px, calc(100vw - 32px));
+  max-height: calc(100vh - 2 * var(--edge) - 196px); overflow: auto; padding: 22px 26px 26px; display: grid; gap: 22px;

+  --feather: linear-gradient(to right, transparent, #000 28px, #000 calc(100% - 12px), transparent), linear-gradient(to bottom, transparent, #000 14px, #000 calc(100% - 22px), transparent);
+  -webkit-mask-image: var(--feather); mask-image: var(--feather); -webkit-mask-composite: source-in; mask-composite: intersect;
+  animation: sheet-in var(--med) var(--ease);
@keyframes sheet-in { from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(-6px); } }

.sheet-close { position: absolute; top: 12px; right: 12px; width: 30px; height: 30px; display: grid; place-items: center; border-radius: 8px; color: var(--ink-3); transition: background var(--fast), color var(--fast); }
.sheet-close:hover { background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.07); color: var(--ink); }

lines: - **Touch and keyboard:** chips open on tap or Enter; the fold toggle works on tap or Enter; Esc clears everything.
### Inspector Sheet
-- **Corner Style:** 10px. **Background:** glass with 16px blur and a hairline border. **Shadow:** Float.

+- **Field:** top-right under the Audit pill, 440px wide like the audit trail. No box, border, corner or shadow: the same frameless dark field as the audit trail and the dock (86% black, 10px blur) that feathers out at its edges, so content scrolling past the top or bottom fades into the volume.
+- **Findings and notes inside** ("What the AI found", area notes) are not boxed either: each hangs off a hairline rail (1px hair-2 on the left, 12px indent), like the audit trail.
- **Head:** the layer name with its glyph (12px/600) and one ink-3 line saying what the ring encodes.
- **Body:** a title or the customer quote, an optional instrument figure, then a two-column fact grid (micro label over 13px ink-2 value).
- **Close:** a 30px square icon button, 8px radius, ink-3 to ink on hover with a 7% white wash. Esc closes; clicking empty space closes.
- 2026-10-11 — Scan filter bar always shown with a fold/unfold toggle (unused chips hide, chips in use stay); new filters: comment length, research topic + fact type, option availability.
- 2026-10-11 — Bottom-left dock: Guide and Agent are now pills like the Audit button; one panel open at a time.
- 2026-10-11 — D-045: audit trail separated by checkpoint; pre-rebuild history hidden by default (toggle in Everything), nothing deleted.
+- 2026-10-11 — Inspector (top-right) moved to the frameless feathered field like the audit trail and dock; findings inside hang off a hairline rail.
- 2026-10-11 — Renamed the app to "SharkSight": one-line geometric shark-head logo + favicon, wordmark beside the page tabs; top-bar pills 28 → 32px (D-044). No LLM spend.

- 2026-10-11 — Sales verification (research/sales-verification.md): ingest correct (36/36); BMW market split implausible (G60 US ~3× public, G68 CN −21–39 %, 5 Series total matches); ~9 duplicated research claims; Q-015 note added. Recommendation: BMW sales only as a labelled relative weight, never as a trend.

lines: **Creative North Star: "Track-While-Scan"**

-The whole interface is a scan volume. A true-black field holds every piece of raw evidence as a contact in one fixed 3D space; each checkpoint is a sweep that passes through that space, and the screen shows what the sweep acquired and how existing tracks changed. The 3D canvas is the page. Everything else sits at the edges of the volume: the readout, the filter chips and the checkpoint timeline as frameless text and marks straight on the black, the inspector and the hover card as small sheets of tinted glass, so the evidence is never boxed into cards or framed by chrome.

+The whole interface is a scan volume. A true-black field holds every piece of raw evidence as a contact in one fixed 3D space; each checkpoint is a sweep that passes through that space, and the screen shows what the sweep acquired and how existing tracks changed. The 3D canvas is the page. Everything else sits at the edges of the volume: the readout, the filter chips and the checkpoint timeline as frameless text and marks straight on the black, the inspector, audit trail and guide dock on a frameless dark field that feathers into the volume, the hover card as a small sheet of tinted glass, so the evidence is never boxed into cards or framed by chrome.

Density sits in the contacts, not in the text. Numerals carry the information, set wide, light and tabular like instrument readouts; words are short labels. The only running text is the customer's own words, shown in the inspector at reading size. Colour is categorical and earned: each raw data type has its own hue, one blue belongs to the sweep and the PM's current position, and amber is held back for loss. State is carried by mark shape, never by hue alone.
**Key Characteristics:**
- True black ground (#000) with the live 3D canvas full-bleed behind every overlay.
-- Overlays pinned to the 24px edge: readout with the filter chips under it top-left, checkpoint timeline bottom-right (both frameless), inspector top-right (glass).
+- Overlays pinned to the 24px edge: readout with the filter chips under it top-left, checkpoint timeline bottom-right (both frameless), inspector top-right (frameless feathered field).
- Wide, light, tabular numerals as the primary text.
- Five categorical data-type hues, one sweep blue, amber reserved for loss.
- Mark shape encodes track state: dot = held, ring = acquired by this sweep.
## Elevation & Depth

-Depth comes from the scene, not from a shadow scale. Contacts fade with distance in the shader, and panels separate from the volume by smoked glass plus backdrop blur (12px for the hover card and page switch, 16px for the inspector) and a hairline border. Floating panels carry one soft, two-layer black shadow so they lift off bright contacts behind them; nothing on the black field sits on a surface lighter than glass.

+Depth comes from the scene, not from a shadow scale. Floating panels carry one soft, two-layer black shadow so they lift off bright contacts behind them; nothing on the black field sits on a surface lighter than glass.

content.text:
Sağ üstte açılan panel (Inspector) artık yeni tasarıma uygun. Evidence'ta bir müşteri yorumuna tıklayıp tarayıcıda kontrol ettim.

- **Panel:** Kutu, çerçeve, köşe yuvarlatma ve gölge kaldırıldı. Audit trail ve sol alttaki Guide/Agent paneliyle aynı koyu, çerçevesiz zemine geçti. Kenarları yumuşakça kayboluyor, kaydırınca içerik üstte ve altta sahneye karışıyor. Genişliği audit paneliyle aynı (440px), yeri değişmedi.
- **İçindeki kartlar:** "What the AI found" bulguları ve area notları da artık kutu içinde değil; audit trail'deki gibi ince bir sol çizgiye asılı duruyor. Bu stil sadece panelin içinde geçerli. Structure sayfasındaki panel de aynı kuralları kullandığı için orada da aynı görünür.
- **Değişmeyen:** Mouse'u bir noktanın üzerine getirince çıkan küçük hover kartını değiştirmedim; hâlâ cam görünümlü. İstersen onu da aynı stile çekerim.

Değişiklik sadece `scan.css`'te. ehl-munich-final-99'un `structure.css` dosyasına dokunmadım. İki oturumun da o sırada bu dosyalarda çalışmadığını önceden teyit ettim. ehl-munich-final-ed şu an AreaBody'yi düzenliyor; ona panele yeni kutu eklememesini, aynı çizgi stilini kullanmasını söyledim. `DESIGN.md`'de Inspector bölümünü ve genel bakışta paneli hâlâ cam olarak anlatan satırları güncelledim; `foundation/STATE.md`'ye log satırı ekledim. Commit yapılmadı.

lines: **Creative North Star: "Track-While-Scan"**

-The whole interface is a scan volume. A true-black field holds every piece of raw evidence as a contact in one fixed 3D space; each checkpoint is a sweep that passes through that space, and the screen shows what the sweep acquired and how existing tracks changed. The 3D canvas is the page. +The whole interface is a scan volume. A true-black field holds every piece of raw evidence as a contact in one fixed 3D space; each checkpoint is a sweep that passes through that space, and the screen shows what the sweep acquired and how existing tracks changed. The 3D canvas is the page. Everything else sits at the edges of the volume: the readout, the filter chips and the checkpoint timeline as frameless text and marks straight on the black, the inspector, audit trail and guide dock on a frameless dark field that feathers into the volume, the hover card on the same field, so the evidence is never boxed into cards or framed by chrome.

Density sits in the contacts, not in the text. Numerals carry the information, set wide, light and tabular like instrument readouts; words are short labels. The only running text is the customer's own words, shown in the inspector at reading size. Colour is categorical and earned: each raw data type has its own hue, one blue belongs to the sweep and the PM's current position, and amber is held back for loss. State is carried by mark shape, never by hue alone.

-Depth comes from the scene, not from a shadow scale. Contacts fade with distance in the shader, and panels separate from the volume by smoked glass plus backdrop blur (12px for the hover card and page switch) and a hairline border; the inspector, audit trail and dock instead sit on a frameless 78–86% black field with a feathered edge. Floating panels carry one soft, two-layer black shadow so they lift off bright contacts behind them; nothing on the black field sits on a surface lighter than glass.

-Depth comes from the scene, not from a shadow scale. Contacts fade with distance in the shader, and panels separate from the volume by smoked glass plus backdrop blur (12px for the page switch) and a hairline border; the inspector, hover card, audit trail and dock instead sit on a frameless 78–86% black field with a feathered edge. Contacts fade with distance in the shader, and panels separate from the volume by smoked glass plus backdrop blur (12px for the page switch) and a hairline border; the inspector, hover card, filter value list, audit trail and dock instead sit on a frameless 78–86% black field with a feathered edge and no shadow; nothing on the black field sits on a surface lighter than glass.
### Shadow Vocabulary

-- **Float Small** (`box-shadow: 0 2px 6px rgba(0,0,0,.5), 0 16px 40px rgba(0,0,0,.5)`): the filter value list, the only glass panel left. The inspector, hover card, audit trail and dock carry no shadow: their feathered dark field separates them from the volume.

+None. The inspector, hover card, filter value list, audit trail and dock carry no shadow: their feathered dark field (86% black, blur) separates them from the volume. Only the page switch keeps glass and a hairline border.
### Named Rules

-**The Glass Over Canvas Rule.** Every panel is translucent over the live volume with a blur: a frameless feathered dark field (inspector, hover card, audit trail, dock) or, for the filter value list, glass. No opaque panels, no solid sidebars. Instruments that are only labels, numerals and marks (readout, filter chips, checkpoint timeline) need no panel at all and sit straight on the black.

+**The Glass Over Canvas Rule.** Every panel is translucent over the live volume with a blur: a frameless feathered dark field (inspector, hover card, filter value list, audit trail, dock). No opaque panels, no solid sidebars. Instruments that are only labels, numerals and marks (readout, filter chips, checkpoint timeline) need no panel at all and sit straight on the black.
## Shapes
A row of chips directly under the readout, one per dimension, any number active at once (values within a dimension are alternatives, dimensions combine).

- **Always shown:** every chip is on the row, the ones in use first in the order they were set (so choosing a value never moves a set chip), then the unused ones. A chip in use shows its dimension in ink-3, the chosen value in ink (first value, "+n" for more) and an ×; a sweep-hi hairline border marks it as set. A "Clear all · Esc" text button follows once anything is set.

- **Fold toggle:** a 28px pill at the head of the row (sliders icon + chevrons, ink-3, hairline on hover). Folding hides the unused chips only (chips in use stay, so nothing is filtered unseen) and the toggle reads "Filter · n" with a chevrons-right; unfolding brings them back to the right. The choice is kept per browser.

-- **Values:** hovering a chip opens its values in a glass list hanging under it: a micro scope line (what this dimension filters), then rows of name, a 2px bar and a tabular count; chosen rows in ink with a sweep-hi bar. Choosing a value closes the list again, so only the choice stays on the chip. Counts already apply the other active filters.

Choosing a value closes the list again, so only the choice stays on the chip. Counts already apply the other active filters.

- **Chips:** 28px pills, hairline border on a 60% black fill, 12px ink-2 text. Car and Market filter every data type. The others belong to one type and carry its glyph: Channel, Label, Engine and Length (short under 80 characters, medium to 250, long) for comments; Trust, Topic and Fact type (figure, event, study or rating, policy, trend) for web research; Study result (above / around / below the car × market's average by half a standard deviation); Category and Availability (standard, optional, in a package) for equipment options; Sales year (2024, 2025, 2030 forecast). Items with no value for a global dimension (options have no market, global research has none) stay visible.
- **In the volume:** items the filters leave out dim to about 6–7% and can't be hovered or opened. Page 2 is never filtered.
- **Touch and keyboard:** chips open on tap or Enter; the fold toggle works on tap or Enter; Esc clears everything.

lines: ### Neutral
- **Void** (void): the page and the WebGL clear colour. Never a near-black; pure black is what makes the contacts read as emitters.
-- **Smoked Glass** (glass): every floating panel, always with a backdrop blur over the canvas.
+- **Smoked Glass** (glass): the page switch, with a backdrop blur over the canvas.

+- **Field** (field): every other panel (inspector, hover card, filter values, audit trail, dock). A near-black at 90% (rgb 10 12 16), a touch cooler and lighter than the void, with a faint cool glow from the top centre (7.5% at the top edge, gone by ~70% down), under a 10px blur and a feathered edge. The glow is what separates panels from the volume and from each other; keep it barely visible.
- **Hairline** (hair) and **Strong Hairline** (hair-strong): panel borders, chip outlines, filter bar tracks, the checkpoint rail, the z-bar midline, scrollbars, mobile pill outlines.
- **Ink** (ink): numerals, titles, the customer quote, active labels, the held mark.
- **Ink 2** (ink-2): secondary values, filter names and counts, ring labels, the checkpoint fill.
## Elevation & Depth

-Depth comes from the scene, not from a shadow scale. Contacts fade with distance in the shader, and panels separate from the volume by smoked glass plus backdrop blur (12px for the page switch) and a hairline border; the inspector, hover card, filter value list, audit trail and dock instead sit on a frameless 78–86% black field with a feathered edge and no shadow; nothing on the black field sits on a surface lighter than glass.

+Depth comes from the scene, not from a shadow scale. Contacts fade with distance in the shader, and panels separate from the volume by smoked glass plus backdrop blur (12px for the page switch) and a hairline border; the inspector, hover card, filter value list, audit trail and dock instead sit on a frameless field (the `field` token: 90% cool near-black with a faint top glow) with a feathered edge and no shadow; nothing on the black field sits on a surface lighter than glass.
### Shadow Vocabulary

-None. The inspector, hover card, filter value list, audit trail and dock carry no shadow: their feathered dark field (86% black, blur) separates them from the volume. Only the page switch keeps glass and a hairline border.

+None. The inspector, hover card, filter value list, audit trail and dock carry no shadow: their feathered field (the `field` token, with its faint top glow) separates them from the volume. Only the page switch keeps glass and a hairline border.
### Named Rules

**The Glass Over Canvas Rule.** Every panel is translucent over the live volume with a blur: a frameless feathered dark field (inspector, hover card, filter value list, audit trail, dock). No opaque panels, no solid sidebars. Instruments that are only labels, numerals and marks (readout, filter chips, checkpoint timeline) need no panel at all and sit straight on the black.
- **Touch and keyboard:** chips open on tap or Enter; the fold toggle works on tap or Enter; Esc clears everything.
### Inspector Sheet

-- **Field:** top-right under the Audit pill, 440px wide like the audit trail. No box, border, corner or shadow: the same frameless dark field as the audit trail and the dock (86% black, 10px blur) that feathers out at its edges, so content scrolling past the top or bottom fades into the volume.

+- **Field:** top-right under the Audit pill, 440px wide like the audit trail. No box, border, corner or shadow: the same frameless field as the audit trail and the dock (the `field` token, 10px blur) that feathers out at its edges, so content scrolling past the top or bottom fades into the volume.
- **Findings and notes inside** ("What the AI found", area notes) are not boxed either: each hangs off a hairline rail (1px hair-2 on the left, 12px indent), like the audit trail.
- **Head:** the layer name with its glyph (12px/600) and one ink-3 line saying what the ring encodes.
- **Body:** a title or the customer quote, an optional instrument figure, then a two-column fact grid (micro label over 13px ink-2 value).

- **Inspector companion:** research, study and option items show "Used as evidence": the themes the AI linked them to at this checkpoint, the relation as a tag (dashed for contradicts) and the AI's one-line reason.
### Hover Card

-320px card following the pointer, on the same frameless dark field as the inspector (86% black, 10px blur, feathered edges, no border or shadow): up to three lines of 13px text, then a micro meta row that leads with the track mark (dot or ring). Pointer events off.

### Range Ring Labels
Billboarded in 3D: car name at 12px/600 ink-2 over its code at micro. Ring name tags are micro text with a 6px colour dot on a 70% black chip (4px radius).

content.text:
I read "blow" as "glow". Tell me if you meant something else, like more blur.

All the panels now have a very faint glow, so they stand out from the 3D view and from each other. I checked in the browser with the inspector and the Guide open at the same time; both now read as separate fields.

- **What changed:** the panel background is no longer pure black. It's a near-black a touch cooler and lighter than the 3D view's background, with a faint cool glow from the top centre. The edges still fade softly, with no frame or shadow.
- **Why not a glow around the edges:** the soft fading edges are made with a mask, and that mask also cuts off anything drawn outside the panel. So the glow is on the panel surface itself.
- **Where it applies:** the right-hand panel, the hover card, the filter value list, the audit trail, and the Guide/Agent panel.
- **One knob:** these panels now share a single colour value, `--field` in `web/src/styles/tokens.css`. If it should be stronger or weaker, it's one number to change.

I also updated the colour section of `DESIGN.md` and the log line in `foundation/STATE.md`. Both other sessions know to use the same colour for any new panels. Nothing is committed.
